findings.description: The instance user_data exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the public web server), leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance's attached storage is created without encryption at rest.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with the credentials placed in user data and the internet-exposed HTTP service, an SSRF flaw could trivially extract them.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and attached to a security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH and HTTP, giving it a directly reachable public address with no bastion or load balancer boundary.
The EBS volume is created with encryption explicitly commented out, so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and is therefore itself unencrypted, allowing data disclosure if the snapshot is copied or shared.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH to the entire internet for brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no HTTPS listener configured, so all traffic to the web host is transmitted in cleartext.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP and is directly internet-reachable, removing the network segmentation boundary.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances in this subnet are automatically assigned public IPs and exposed to the internet.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network flow records (sensitive reconnaissance data) are stored unencrypted.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or ACL controls
findings.description: The bucket defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, versioning, or bucket policy restricting access, leaving flow log data at risk of accidental public exposure and undetectable tampering/deletion (force_destroy is also enabled).
